facts.fact: The Roadmap's table of digital health tools, from the Ministry's landscape assessment of 15-29 November 2022, lists DHIS2 as the Health Management Information System, deployed by the MoH in all districts and at the 'scaled' stage.

The National Digital Health Roadmap 2024-2026, the Ministry's guiding document for three years, carries a section on the District Health Management Information System (3.5.1) under Services and Applications, which takes NLe 142.5 million (US$6.07 million, 63.6%) of an indicative US$10.0 million costing; the section's text is outside the capture. The document gives the span 2024-2026 and no publication day.

The Roadmap states that the digital health interventions assessed in November 2022, DHIS2 among them, were 83% donor driven and 17% private sector funded with no significant public contribution, that only 1% of the US$1.2 million needed for the 2018 strategy was budgeted by the MoH in 2019 and half of that released, and that the MoH's 2022 statutory budget had no provision for digital health. The figure covers all interventions, not DHIS2 alone.

The Roadmap states that DHIS 2 and tracker applications are widely used, with 96% coverage of public health facilities and no corresponding adoption by private facilities, from the MoH landscape assessment of 246 facilities in 16 districts in November 2022. No numerator or denominator is given, the figure joins DHIS2 with tracker applications, covers all public facilities rather than primary clinics, and says 'coverage', not who keys the data.

The Roadmap's table of tools assessed in November 2022 shows EMR at primary level only as pilots: a Facility Management Information System EMR at 1 PHU each in Kambia and Port Loko (GOPA-GIZ, pilot) and Salone EMR at Waterloo PHU (GIZ, pre-implementation); the text says point-of-care solutions including EMR were increasing at pre-implementation and early pilot stages.

facts.fact: The Roadmap describes the EMR systems seen in the November 2022 assessment as point-of-care solutions for the patient care continuum, at pre-implementation and early pilot stages.

Every EMR in the Roadmap's table of tools assessed in November 2022 is deployed by a partner or private body, none by the MoH: CUAMM (Elysium, PCMH), Partners In Health (OpenMRS, Wellbody clinic, Kono), GOPA-GIZ (2 PHUs), GIZ (Salone EMR), UNICEF (OpenMRS, Ola During Children's Hospital), Health Connect (34 Military and Connaught hospitals) and Sierra Rutile Ltd (its own clinic).

The National Digital Health Roadmap 2024-2026 carries a section on Electronic Health Records Systems deployment (3.5.2) and a figure of QEHSSSP 'hub' and 'spokes' facilities; the section's text is outside the capture. The document gives the span 2024-2026 and no publication day.

The Roadmap states that the digital health interventions assessed in November 2022, the EMR pilots among them, were 83% donor driven and 17% private sector funded with no significant public contribution, and that the MoH's 2022 statutory budget had no provision for digital health. The figure covers all interventions, not EMR alone.
